verdicts.reason: Quotes verified verbatim. 16.01.01:220 states 'suppressed from search at the floor (16.01.05 D-03)'; 16.01.05:98 (D-03) says only 'Never-verified seeded records must present as unverified, not open' — no suppression rule. A full grep for 'suppress' across the sub-tree shows 16.01.05's only search-suppression rule attaches to `possibly closed` (:59, :73 — 2 corroborations + 21-day non-response), NOT to the freshness floor. The owning file contradicts :220 outright: 16.05.05:60 'The output is presentation, not suppression'; 16.05.05:99 (DT-02) 'Present with age; never suppress'; D-08 at :127 makes permanent 'never verified' the correct floor; :81 places all trades there permanently; 16.05.01:246 keeps a closed-in-2019 seeded venue presented, not suppressed. So :220's mechanism is both mis-cited and contradicted. DOWNGRADED from blocking: no product behaviour must be invented — the dedicated owner of freshness semantics (16.05.05 DT-02/D-08) states the rule explicitly and negatively, and the cited D-03 visibly does not contain the suppression clause, so an implementer chasing the citation finds the correct rule rather than a fork. The defect is a silent, unmarked false statement in a non-owning file, not an unresolvable divergence.

Quotes verified verbatim (16.05.06:96, :373 D-14, :378 D-19, :294, :225). The arithmetic objection is correct — a monthly cadence is ~3x the 90-day per-room cap — but it lands in a rationale clause, not a normative one, and the resulting behaviour is unambiguous. 16.05.06:91 states 'Two caps, both hard (D-14)'; :96 enumerates the waivers exhaustively ('The 90-day cap is waived when ... independent corroboration of an open contest (rank 1) ... The 7-day cap is never waived'); nothing anywhere grants a lockout exemption. D-19's normative content is only that the billing cycle is the completion-equivalent that 'triggers the harvest' — and :70 puts every trigger through the same two-condition gate ('(a) uncertain field ... (b) The contributor's budget allows it'), so the cap gates delivery regardless of trigger cadence. The file's own user-facing statement at :294 is an upper bound — 'at most one prompt per month' — which one-per-90-days satisfies. Both competent implementers land on: trigger monthly, deliver at most quarterly per room. The residual D-19 mechanism is separately tracked at :399 (Q-08, Agent, /create-prd-architecture, cross-check 16.06.09).

Every quote verified verbatim, and the contradiction is broader than the finding states. Block camp: 16.01.02:181 ('It is a block, not a booking ... no reservation => no proof-of-presence => no harvest trigger', UI 'no post-session prompt'); 16.01.02:239 ('an Operator's own session is a block, not a booking => no harvest trigger'); 16.03.01:202 and :288 (same, 'A block, not a booking (16.01.02) => no reservation => no proof of presence => no harvest'); 16.02.02:169 ('Harvest prompt suppressed for the fields on the room they own'). Reservation camp: 16.06.03:394 (D-12 'a zero-value reservation, not a block'); :349 (DT-12 'REJECTED for a session'); :298 ('Consumes inventory, completes, triggers the harvest and archive policy' / UI 'You'll get the usual prompt after'); :29 Role Lens ('May book their own room as a zero-value reservation'); :230; and 16.05.06:277 + D-11 at :370, which presuppose the harvest DOES fire on an Operator's own booking and merely reclassify it owner-class. DT-12's carve-out is explicitly 'a block is still right for a private event' — an Operator's own band session is not a private event, so it does not reconcile the two. Opposite entities, opposite downstream chains, opposite user-facing copy, no marker on either side. 16.06.03 D-13 lists 'until D-12, the Operator's own session' as closed, proving supersession was intended and never propagated to the room-entity owner. Blocking upheld.

Quote verified verbatim at 16.05.03:65, and Step 5 is confirmed elapsed (16.07:71 'Re-targeted (ideation Step 5 has run and did not take it)'), so the marker is stale. But the outcome the implementer needs is specified twice over. The row's own 'User Sees' column prescribes the state: 'Field shows multiple competing pending edits, both flagged unresolved' — neither applies, current value stands. That is exactly 16.05.04 D-01 (:106): 'Default: last-agreed stands, contest visible. Not owner-wins, not community-wins', whose rationale is provenance-agnostic ('Neither party is trustworthy by default') and whose DT-02 (:88) states the product position explicitly: 'the platform often does not know — and "we do not know, here are both positions" is a legitimate product state, not a failure to design.' What is genuinely absent is only an ARBITRATION model — a mechanism to eventually pick a winner — which is a refinement, not a behaviour the implementer must invent, and whose governing artefact (the field-class -> policy map) is itself tracked at 16.05.04:50 and Q-01, plus 16.05.03 Q-05 (User, /write-be-spec) for the auto-apply cut line that gates D-05 reachability.

All quotes verified verbatim. 16.02.02:176 and :273 assert as fact that 'current room exclusion is binary' and that co-bookable-but-degraded 'has no correct representation' / 'is currently unexpressible'. 16.01.02:67 types `contends` as 'Symmetric | Soft. Both bookable. The second booking is admitted only after the contended facility and its Operator-authored rule are shown and acknowledged; both parties are notified', with the literal example 'Main Room and Basement share one PA — both can trade, but not both loud'; :158 works the identical scenario; D-06 at :269 and D-07 at :270 ratify it. So the platform demonstrably CAN express the state, and the second booking is caught at calendar time — directly refuting ':273's PA conflict that no calendar will catch'. The cross-reference is also confirmed wrong: 16.01.02 Q-01 at :285 is '[OWNER] Delegated-room economics (D-09)', unrelated to exclusion — corroborating that the 16.02.02 text predates D-06 and was never refreshed. Q-08's tracking (Agent, /create-prd-architecture, 'cross-check with 16.01.02 and 16.06.01') mitigates but does not cure: the tracking rests on a false premise and cites a question that does not exist as described. Warning is the right level — the risk is a duplicated shared-resource entity at architecture time, not an unimplementable spec.

Every quote verified verbatim. 16.06-cx:183 records R-05 as 'Rejected for this pass as unresolved rather than absent — 16.06.09 Q-04 asks exactly this ... rather than confirming a relationship the model cannot yet support.' Both premises are false against the child: 16.06.09:128 (D-05) 'A skipped recurring instance is released to the waitlist (16.06.04)'; :78 'the single instance is marked skipped and offered to the waitlist (16.06.04) as one-off inventory'; :114 Cross-Cut Notes already record the touch to 16.06.04; and Q-04 at :137 is struck through as RESOLVED and concerns external-calendar recurrence reconciliation, asking nothing about waitlist backfill. So the sub-domain's cross-cut map — the artefact whose stated job is enumerating which children interact — denies a relationship its own child ratifies as a decision, and routes the reader to a resolved question about a different subject. Unmarked and stale. Warning, not blocking: D-05 is normative and unambiguous, so an implementer reading the child wires it correctly; the harm is a downstream stage trusting the dependency map.

Quotes verified verbatim. 16.01.05:31-32 declares the status vocabulary as a closed list — 'Status is a small state machine on the place record: `open` · `temporarily closed` · `permanently closed` · `relocated`' — and it is the file's only normative statement of that enum. D-06 at :100 mandates 'The auto-flip to `possibly closed`', :59 confirms it is a status transition in the same machine ('flips the record to `possibly closed` (never to `permanently closed` — that stays Operator-only)'), and the States table at :73 gives it a distinct trigger and distinct behaviour ('suppressed in search until re-verified') that none of the four listed values carries. Two normative statements that cannot both hold, with no marker on either. Unlike finding #007 there is no struck-through RESOLVED record or supersession note flagging the enumeration as stale — the Behavior sentence simply reads as authoritative and complete. Warning is correct: the value and its semantics are fully specified at :73/:100 so nothing must be invented, but a BE spec author quoting the vocabulary declaration ships a four-value enum with nowhere to put D-06's state.

Quotes verified verbatim at 16.01-cx:128-131, and the Step-5 target is elapsed. But the substantive question is not live, because the state it posits is not reachable. A grep of 16.01.06 returns ZERO occurrences of 'licence review' or 'at-risk': D-06 (:152) locks five statutory slots — occupancy ceiling, liability cover, electrical/fire-safety record, performing-rights licence status, hirer requirements — and a licence review is none of them. There is therefore no 16.01.06 record that could emit the signal, and no 'one write, two surfaces' fork to decide. Meanwhile the at-risk authoring model is completely specified in 16.01.05: the Role Lens (:22) gives the Operator 'Can declare at-risk themselves (a licence review, a redevelopment notice)'; Musician/Producer report it (:24-26); the Happy Path (:47-51) walks report -> flag -> Operator confirm/correct/dispute -> public; D-02 (:97) fixes the write asymmetry and D-05 (:100) owns the reason enum. CX-05 itself records only 'Medium confidence' and speculates the overlap 'MAY indicate the statutory record should emit at-risk signals rather than duplicate them' — a flagged architectural refinement note, not a behaviour gap. An implementer builds 16.01.05's human-authored flow and is never blocked.
